checks.claim: OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors are generally better than 0.008 m in plan.
OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors are generally better than 0.020 m in height.
OSTN15 defines OSGB36 National Grid in conjunction with OS Net stations.
OSTN15 agreement with old triangulation network stations is about 0.1 m RMS for Great Britain.
OSGM15 standard error in height for Great Britain is 0.008 m.
OS states 1-2 cm positional accuracy can be achievable using suitable GNSS with OS Net corrections.
GNSS and OS mapping use different Earth models and coordinate systems.
GPS commonly uses WGS84 whereas OS mapping uses OSGB36 National Grid.
OS mapping heights use Ordnance Datum Newlyn for Great Britain.
OSTN15/OSGM15 are the national standard transformations between GNSS coordinates and OSGB36/mean-sea-level heights.
OSTN15 models horizontal transformation to and from OSGB36 National Grid.
OSGM15 models transformation to and from mean-sea-level-based heights.
